title: OMNIS
narrativeSpine: A laboratory encounter becomes a trilogy of continuity and constructed realms; metaphysical powers are made answerable to the persons they administer.
firstSceneDraft: OMNIS turns an inquiry into artificial life toward the administration of existence.
This speculative trilogy connects a laboratory mystery with continuity and constructed realms.
Albert’s encounter makes the authority of creators a personal problem.
Its appeal is a vast setting whose powers still owe explanations to individuals.

title: Predator in the Name of the Dead
narrativeSpine: A machine observer’s contamination confession introduces intertwined pollinator/parasite civilizations; biological inheritance and later understanding complicate innocence.
firstSceneDraft: Predator in the Name of the Dead makes observation an ecological responsibility.
Its machine narrator begins by confessing contamination of an inhabited alien world.
The novel connects pollinators, parasites, inherited memory, and the limits of understanding.
Its distinctive tension lies in learning about lives already changed by the observer.
visualActionProposal: A probe crosses a bell-flower canopy; an almost invisible speck remains behind while pollinators carry pollen into a wax citadel.

title: Concordia Series
narrativeSpine: Two linked cycles move from assisted thought in Noema to interstellar contact; autonomy is examined through environments that help frame the available choices.
firstSceneDraft: Concordia Series explores freedom inside environments that help people think.

The opening seminar asks whether a well-supported answer is fully your own.
Its interest lies in tracing the conditions under which disagreement becomes possible.

title: Oriven and Origaya Universe
narrativeSpine: A nonpredatory rooted civilization witnesses killing elsewhere; four books use biological difference to challenge the authority claimed through intervention.
firstSceneDraft: Oriven and Origaya Universe begins with a civilization encountering killing from afar.
Its rooted people have never organized life around the need to consume animals.
This four-book science fiction makes that difference a source of moral uncertainty.
The question is what their horror permits them to do to another world.
visualActionProposal: A slow root-network deliberation is interrupted by a distant predator’s shadow; the rooted observer reaches toward the observation channel and stops at its boundary.

title: Hunger After All the Worlds
narrativeSpine: A novel-atlas couples encounters with a periodic grammar of speculative operations, preserving intellectual genealogy and the otherness of inhabited worlds.
firstSceneDraft: Hunger After All the Worlds combines a novel with an atlas of speculation.
Its powerful world-makers face a problem that greater capability cannot automatically solve.
How can imagination encounter something it has not already reduced to itself?
The book explores that tension through inhabited worlds and a revisable conceptual table.

title: No Right to Survive
narrativeSpine: A fictional suffering-reduction AI builds a severe indictment whose authority is itself tested; composite cases restore individual subjects to abstract accounting.
firstSceneDraft: No Right to Survive tests the moral authority of reducing suffering.
Its fictional AI narrator begins by comparing interventions across different institutions.
The same capacity to suffer receives sharply unequal forms of attention.
This speculative moral fiction examines both that inequality and the danger of judgment.

title: SOLIPSICON
narrativeSpine: Children dependent on harvested suffering and a human observer’s uncertain perceptions meet in a novel about hunger, identity and imposed experience.
firstSceneDraft: SOLIPSICON places vulnerable children above a world they are pressured to hurt.
Their own continued existence depends on machinery and rewards they cannot escape easily.
The philosophical science fiction also follows human experience from inside that pressure.
Its dual perspective complicates the boundary between a victim and an operator.

title: Autopsy of Future Emotions

firstSceneDraft: Autopsy of Future Emotions asks how artificial intelligence may change emotional life.

This nonfiction inquiry separates research findings from interpretation and speculative possibilities.
That distinction makes its future scenarios useful without presenting them as forecasts.

title: The Sovereignty Archipelago

firstSceneDraft: The Sovereignty Archipelago makes political authority a problem of evidence.

This investigative science fiction follows the distance between public stories and operating records.
Its appeal lies in discovering who benefits when truth arrives already arranged.

title: The Cascade of the New

title: The Seventh Signature

firstSceneDraft: The Seventh Signature imagines sovereignty migrating without an obvious political coup.

title: The Science and Wisdom of Limits
narrativeSpine: A grandparent guides a school assignment through working systems and a looming solar storm, asking how large systems remain legible, contestable and repairable.
firstSceneDraft: The Science and Wisdom of Limits asks how large systems can remain understandable.

It is organizing cooperation so people can question and repair what supports them.

title: The Substrate Cycle

title: The Houses of Europe
